findings.summary: D-11 provider_pool_share uses max(1, pool_size(PROVIDER)//n) but pool_size(PROVIDER)==workers(), so the floor contradicts the boot assertion sum(shares)<=pool_size; T-life-1 'n in 1..8' is false for small contracts; and build_routed_provider cannot verify the connections of already-built clients. Drop the floor (raise CapacityUnavailable when share<1), bound the test, and make the budget checkable (factory or connections property).
Router total_s is per attempt while the edge max-duration deadline is from stream start, so after a fallback the edge can win the race; P11 claim is wrong for that case.
Zero-provider-call refusals inside open_routed (all_unavailable, snapshot_unavailable, etc.) occur after mark_dispatched, so the budget spend is not refunded, unlike preflight refusals.
D-9 gap tightening (1s to 0.8s) also affects routed streaming, not only non-streaming; state it in D-9 and the PR notice.
Candidate ids appear in deciding_rule inside the client-visible response body; state they are org-owned or hash them.
